narrativeReportMd:
# Dosage R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Dosage` has several local R4-to-R6 instance-breaking changes: `sequence` was removed, `asNeeded[x]` was split, `site` changed JSON shape from `CodeableConcept` to `CodeableReference`, and the three `maxDosePer*` fields were replaced by `safety.doseLimit`. R6 also adds expressive content that is not cleanly representable in R4, especially `condition`, formula-based dose/rate `Expression` choices, and expanded `DosageSafety` content.

## Scope
The report covers the core datatype `StructureDefinition/Dosage` and uses R6 `DosageSafety`, `DosageCondition`, and `DosageDetails` as supporting inputs. Inherited `BackboneElement` to `BackboneType` and base `Element`/`Extension` constraint presentation changes are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
The largest theme is structural migration rather than mere code-system change: old JSON members must be renamed, wrapped, or moved. Several R4 fields had compact representations that R6 moved into more expressive substructures. Reverse conversion from R6 to R4 can be lossy because R6 permits multiple as-needed reasons, BodyStructure references, formula expressions, conditions, multiple safety dose limits, and instructions for exceeding safety limits.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact local findings are the `maxDosePer*` redesign into `Dosage.safety`, the `site` change to `CodeableReference`, and the `asNeeded[x]` split with the new `dos-1` invariant. These affect validation, generated models, and conversion transforms.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important when migrating sequencing semantics, dose-limit safety semantics, condition-driven applicability, reference-only body sites, and Expression-based dose/rate formulas.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most changes appear aimed at supporting richer R6 modeling, but several could have been staged less disruptively by preserving old elements as deprecated aliases or adding optional parallel elements before removal.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate reviews of `BackboneType`, `DosageSafety`, `DosageCondition`, `DosageDetails`, and the external dose-rate terminology would improve cross-artifact migration planning.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Dosage` has hard local R4-to-R6 breaks caused by removed or reshaped fields, plus high reverse-conversion risk for new R6 conditional and safety constructs. The top migration concerns are `maxDosePer*` to `safety.doseLimit`, `site` to `CodeableReference`, and `asNeeded[x]` to `asNeeded`/`asNeededFor`. The main uncertainty is terminology/narrative intent because official diffs and expansions were not available locally.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be implemented as an explicit structural transform, not as a permissive parser update. R4 `sequence`, `asNeededCodeableConcept`, `site`, and `maxDosePer*` payloads will not validate as-is against the R6 Dosage shape. Reverse conversion needs policy decisions for R6 content that has no R4 home, including multiple safety limits, `condition`, `BodyStructure` references, and `Expression`-based formulas.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for element presence, cardinality, type, flag, and binding deltas because they come directly from the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions. Confidence is lower for the rationale and terminology consequences because no official diff, narrative pages, or live terminology expansions were used.

findings.title: Dosage.sequence was removed

semanticText.short: The order of the dosage instructions
semanticText.definition: Indicates the order in which the dosage instructions should be applied or interpreted.
semanticText.requirements: If sequence numbers are the same, Dosages are concurrent; if different, Dosages are sequential.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed `Dosage.sequence` to express ordering and concurrency among multiple dosage instructions.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 `Dosage` has no local replacement field for this sequence number. More complex step ordering appears to be modeled outside this datatype, for example in the separate `DosageDetails` structure.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: No R6 element with the same path or a simple renamed path exists under `Dosage`; sequencing is not represented as a local Dosage child in R6.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance containing `sequence` has a member that is not allowed by the R6 `Dosage` StructureDefinition. Generated R6 models also will not expose this property, so code that sorts or groups dosage instructions by `sequence` needs a new source of ordering semantics.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Losing sequential-versus-concurrent dosing semantics can change how tapering, alternating, or multi-step instructions are interpreted.

justification.inferredGoal: Move ordering semantics out of the simple Dosage datatype into richer dosage-course modeling.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain optional `Dosage.sequence` as deprecated while adding or promoting richer course or step modeling elsewhere.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of moving beyond a single integer sequence toward richer dosage-course modeling is reasonable, but the supplied evidence does not show that removing the optional R4 field from base `Dosage` was necessary to achieve it. Keeping `sequence` would preserve R4-valid instances and generated APIs while still allowing R6 systems to prefer newer course or step constructs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have left `Dosage.sequence` at `0..1 integer`, marked it deprecated, clarified that it is only a legacy ordering/concurrency hint, and directed richer sequencing to the relevant R6 course structure. The main cost is lingering legacy semantics and potential precedence rules when both old and new ordering mechanisms are present, but that does not appear to defeat the core R6 goal.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Low-to-moderate tradeoff: preserves a weak legacy ordering field and needs precedence guidance if an enclosing course structure also carries order.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Dosage.sequence` as 0..1 integer with summary flag true.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment illustrates the removed member; it is not intended to be a complete standalone resource.

findings.narrativeMd: `Dosage.sequence` was a compact way to say whether multiple dosage instructions were sequential or concurrent. Its removal is a direct instance break for any R4 dosage carrying the field and a runtime break for code that used it to order instructions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 data with `sequence` is old-valid/new-invalid unless the member is removed or moved to an enclosing R6 construct. This is primarily an R4-to-R6 validation and codegen break; R6-to-R4 representability is not the issue because R6 no longer has the field.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not simply drop `sequence` without reviewing the containing resource. If the sequence encoded clinically meaningful order or concurrency, migrate that meaning into the R6 container, an R6 `DosageDetails` course structure where applicable, or an extension/profile-specific rule. Test examples with same sequence, different sequence, and omitted sequence.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was probably intended to consolidate sequence semantics into richer dose-course modeling, but it could have been introduced compatibly by retaining `sequence` as deprecated. The tradeoff would be model duplication and possible disagreement between old and new ordering fields.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The exact R6 migration target depends on the resource or profile containing the Dosage array, which was outside this artifact-scoped review.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Dosage.sequence` was an optional integer used to distinguish ordered versus concurrent dosage instructions. R6 removes the local element entirely; a raw R4 dosage carrying `sequence` is not valid R6 Dosage content, and an implementation that used it to interpret tapers, alternating doses, or grouped instructions needs an explicit replacement policy. The R6 `DosageDetails.step` model suggests a richer course representation, but it is not a same-path compatibility bridge for existing Dosage arrays.
keyEvidence: R4 `StructureDefinition-Dosage.json` snapshot has `Dosage.sequence` 0..1 integer, isSummary true, with requirements for concurrent versus sequential Dosages.
R6 `StructureDefinition-DosageDetails.json` has `step` for dosage-course sequencing, but it is a separate datatype with required `renderedInstruction` and nested `step.component` Dosage content.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The supplied R4 status is trial-use and the local maturity map gives Dosage `standardsStatus: trial-use` with no numeric FMM, so I did not treat this as a normative-stability violation. However, Dosage is used by medication resources with FMM 2-3 locally, and ordering of medication instructions can be safety-relevant, so trial-use status only partly softens the concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance with `sequence` has an element absent from R6; runtime/API/codegen also changes because R6 models no longer expose the property.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A plausible less-breaking base design was to keep `Dosage.sequence` as a deprecated 0..1 legacy ordering hint while adding richer course modeling elsewhere. The tradeoff is some duplicated ordering semantics and precedence guidance, but for this narrow field that cost appears modest compared with dropping a clinically meaningful hint.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly identifies a hard instance break and a plausible less-breaking alternative; my fresh review likewise treats the removal as deserving renewed design attention.

findings.title: Dosage.asNeeded[x] was split into asNeeded and repeating asNeededFor

oldState.summary: Optional choice element allowing boolean or CodeableConcept.

binding.description: A coded concept identifying the precondition that should be met before consuming or administering a medication dose.

semanticText.definition: Indicates whether the Medication is only taken when needed within a specific dosing schedule, or indicates the precondition for taking the Medication.
semanticText.comment: A CodeableConcept implied true; boolean false meant the dose was scheduled and not as needed.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented both the PRN boolean and the reason/precondition as one choice element.

newState.summary: Boolean is now `asNeeded`; reasons are `asNeededFor` 0..* CodeableConcept, constrained by root invariant `dos-1`.

binding.description: A coded concept identifying the precondition that should be met before consuming or administering a medication dose.

constraints.human: AsNeededFor can only be set if AsNeeded is empty or true

semanticText.definition: `asNeeded` indicates the boolean flag; `asNeededFor` contains CodeableConcept preconditions.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 separates the boolean and reason concepts and allows multiple as-needed reasons.

facts.newValue: dos-1: asNeededFor.empty() or asNeeded.empty() or asNeeded

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The name, definitions, binding, and mappings show that R6 `asNeeded` and `asNeededFor` split the two R4 choice branches.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 JSON uses choice member names such as `asNeededBoolean` and `asNeededCodeableConcept`; R6 expects `asNeeded` and `asNeededFor`. R4 `asNeededCodeableConcept` is therefore invalid unless transformed. Reverse conversion is lossy when R6 carries multiple `asNeededFor` reasons because R4 allowed only one CodeableConcept choice.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Mis-mapping PRN status or reason can change when a medication should be taken.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate the as-needed boolean from one or more coded reasons and make their relationship explicit.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated `asNeeded[x]` and add repeating `asNeededFor`, with invariants or guidance for conflicts.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating the PRN flag from one or more reasons is a reasonable R6 goal, and the `dos-1` invariant makes the false-with-reason case computable. A less-breaking design exists, but it would preserve the overloaded R4 choice and create two same-resource ways to communicate as-needed reasons, so the chosen break is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial alternative would have retained `asNeeded[x]` for R4 JSON compatibility while adding `asNeededFor` for multiple coded preconditions. That would preserve old instances, but validators and converters would need rules for `asNeededBoolean=false` with reasons, for `asNeededCodeableConcept` versus `asNeededFor`, and for duplicate or conflicting reason content. The alternative only partly meets the cleanup goal because deprecated PRN representations could persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Material duplication: PRN boolean and reason semantics would exist in both the old overloaded choice and the new repeating reason field.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `asNeeded[x]` as 0..1 boolean or CodeableConcept.
R6 defines separate `asNeeded` boolean and repeating `asNeededFor` CodeableConcept elements.
R6 adds an error invariant preventing `asNeededFor` when `asNeeded` is false.

examples.examplesMd: R4 `asNeededBoolean` maps mechanically to R6 `asNeeded`. R4 `asNeededCodeableConcept` should map to one `asNeededFor` entry and usually `asNeeded: true` or omitted; setting `asNeeded: false` with `asNeededFor` violates `dos-1`.

findings.narrativeMd: `asNeeded[x]` changed from a two-branch choice into two separate fields. This breaks JSON shape and generated choice-property APIs, but it also clarifies semantics by allowing multiple reasons and by forbidding reasons when `asNeeded` is false.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with `asNeededCodeableConcept` is invalid in R6 until transformed to `asNeededFor`. An R4 instance with `asNeededBoolean` is also invalid as raw JSON because R6 uses `asNeeded` rather than the R4 choice name. R6 instances with multiple reasons cannot be represented exactly in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `asNeededBoolean` to `asNeeded`. Map `asNeededCodeableConcept` to `asNeededFor[0]` and set `asNeeded` to true unless a local rule intentionally relies on the R6 convention that reasons imply as-needed. Validate migrated records against `dos-1` and test false, true-without-reason, reason-without-boolean, and multiple-reason cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The split is understandable because it removes an overloaded choice and supports multiple reasons. A backward-compatible alternative would have kept `asNeeded[x]` as deprecated while introducing `asNeededFor`, but that would have prolonged ambiguity and duplicated PRN semantics.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 used one choice element, serialized as `asNeededBoolean` or `asNeededCodeableConcept`. R6 separates that into `asNeeded` boolean and repeating `asNeededFor` CodeableConcept, with an invariant that reasons cannot accompany `asNeeded=false`. This is a real wire-format and generated-model break, but it also removes an overloaded choice, permits multiple reasons, and makes the false-with-reason case computably invalid.
keyEvidence: R4 `Dosage.asNeeded[x]` is 0..1 with boolean and CodeableConcept choices.
R6 `Dosage.asNeeded` is 0..1 boolean and `Dosage.asNeededFor` is 0..* CodeableConcept with the same medication-as-needed-reason example binding.
R6 root invariant `dos-1` is severity error with expression `asNeededFor.empty() or asNeeded.empty() or asNeeded`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Trial-use status lowers the compatibility burden compared with normative content, but PRN medication instructions are central enough that the break still matters. The judgment is not softened to `No problem` because existing R4 wire names and generated APIs do need transformation.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 choice members `asNeededBoolean` and `asNeededCodeableConcept` are not the R6 member names; R6-to-R4 loss can also occur when multiple `asNeededFor` reasons are present.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial less-breaking design could have kept deprecated `asNeeded[x]` while adding `asNeededFor`, but that would preserve two representations for PRN status and reasons in the base datatype and require conflict handling. Those tradeoffs are material enough that the cleaner R6 split appears proportionate.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's hard/high impact and partial-alternative assessment are consistent with the evidence, though the final judgment emphasizes that the break is probably justified.

findings.title: Dosage.site changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference(BodyStructure)

binding.description: A coded concept describing the site location the medicine enters into or onto the body.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented the administration site directly as a CodeableConcept at `site`.

binding.description: A coded concept describing the site location the medicine enters into or onto the body.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 represents the site as a `CodeableReference`, which can carry either `concept` or a reference to a `BodyStructure`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element path is unchanged, but the datatype changes and R6 adds a BodyStructure target profile.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The R4 JSON shape `site.coding` is not the R6 `CodeableReference` shape; a forward transform must wrap it under `site.concept`. Reverse conversion is not always lossless because R6 may use `site.reference` to point to a BodyStructure with details that are not present as a simple code.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Administration site can be clinically relevant for route, laterality, device placement, and patient safety.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow a dosage site to be represented either as a code or as a reference to a more precise BodyStructure.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `site` as `CodeableConcept` and add a separate optional BodyStructure reference field.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of supporting either a coded site or a precise `BodyStructure` reference is reasonable and matches the R4 commentary that more precise body-site representation may be needed. A separate reference field would avoid the R4 JSON-shape break, but it would split one clinical fact across parallel fields, so the cleaner `CodeableReference` redesign is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative would keep `Dosage.site` as `CodeableConcept` and add something like `siteReference` for `BodyStructure`, or formalize use of a body-site extension as transition guidance. The extension/backport approach is only a mitigation, not a base-design alternative. The real base alternative has material tradeoffs because it allows two site representations on the same dosage and requires precedence, consistency, and conversion rules.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Material duplication and reconciliation cost: coded and referenced site facts could disagree and generic tooling would not get one unified `CodeableReference` representation.

evidence.detail: R6 type is CodeableReference with target profile BodyStructure.

examples.examplesMd: Forward conversion of a coded R4 site is deterministic: wrap the CodeableConcept in `site.concept`. Reverse conversion needs policy when R6 uses only `site.reference`.

findings.narrativeMd: `Dosage.site` kept the same path but changed datatype. This is easy to miss because the clinical meaning and binding are similar, but the serialized JSON and generated property type are different.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Raw R4 instances with `site.coding` become invalid against R6 because a `CodeableReference` expects `concept` or `reference`. R6 coded concepts can be converted back to R4, but reference-only BodyStructure sites are not cleanly representable without dereferencing, selecting a code, or using an extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap R4 `site` as R6 `site.concept`. For R6-to-R4, define a policy for `site.reference`: resolve BodyStructure and map to a CodeableConcept when possible, preserve as an extension, or reject as not representable. Test coded-only, reference-only, and code-plus-reference cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is likely justified by the need for precise anatomic site references, but a new optional reference field or extension would have avoided changing the JSON shape of existing coded sites. The chosen design is cleaner but breaking.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Dosage.site` kept its path but changed from a direct `CodeableConcept` to `CodeableReference(BodyStructure)`. Existing coded R4 sites require wrapping under `site.concept`, and R6 reference-only body sites cannot always be represented as an R4 code without resolving or losing detail. The change is breaking, but it fits the R6 goal of allowing either a coded site or a precise BodyStructure reference in one field.
keyEvidence: R4 `Dosage.site` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept` with example binding to `approach-site-codes`.
R6 `Dosage.site` is 0..1 `CodeableReference` targeting `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/BodyStructure`, with the same example binding.
R4 and R6 comments both recognize use cases needing precise body-site attributes; R6 makes that reference capability part of the base element.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Trial-use status reduces the presumption against model cleanup. Medication administration site can still be clinically relevant, but the forward migration for coded R4 content is deterministic, so the FMM/status context supports accepting the break if the unified CodeableReference goal is desired.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: raw R4 JSON such as `site.coding` is not the R6 CodeableReference shape; R6-to-R4 loss occurs for `site.reference` when no equivalent CodeableConcept is available.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have left `site` as CodeableConcept and added a separate BodyStructure reference element, but that would split one administration-site fact across parallel fields and require precedence and consistency rules. A `CodeableReference` is a cleaner base model despite the wire-shape migration.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly treats this as a hard/high bidirectional compatibility issue with only a partial less-breaking alternative.

findings.title: maxDosePerPeriod, maxDosePerAdministration, and maxDosePerLifetime were replaced by Dosage.safety.doseLimit

semanticText.definition: Upper limits on medication per unit of time, per administration, or per lifetime.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had separate top-level fields for period, administration, and lifetime maximum doses.

newState.summary: One optional `Dosage.safety` element containing `DosageSafety`; dose limits are represented as repeating `doseLimit` entries.

constraints.human: `DosageSafety.doseLimit.value[x]` is mandatory when a doseLimit entry exists.
`DosageSafety.doseLimit.scope` is mandatory and required-bound to dose-limit-scope.

semanticText.definition: Safety information about the dosage instructions, including dose limits and what to do if exceeded.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 consolidates safety limits under `Dosage.safety`. Each `doseLimit` has required `value[x]` and required `scope`; `ifExceeded` is a root property of `DosageSafety`, not a per-limit child.

facts.newValue: DosageSafety.doseLimit 0..* with value[x] 1..1 integer|Quantity|Expression, scope 1..1 required code, period 0..1 Duration, text 0..1

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The removed R4 fields are semantically dose safety limits. R6 introduces `Dosage.safety` and `DosageSafety.doseLimit` with scopes `period`, `administration`, and `lifetime`, plus a new `dosage` scope.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 Dosage using one of the `maxDosePer*` fields contains members that are absent in R6. Migration must create a nested safety structure and populate required `doseLimit.value[x]` and `doseLimit.scope` fields. Reverse conversion is lossy for R6 dose-limit features outside the three R4 fields.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Maximum dose limits are medication safety controls; losing or mis-scoping them can affect overdose prevention.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize dose safety limits into a reusable structure with multiple limits, scopes, formulas, periods, notes, and exceeded-limit instructions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `Dosage.safety` while retaining deprecated `maxDosePerPeriod`, `maxDosePerAdministration`, and `maxDosePerLifetime` aliases.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Generalizing dose safety limits into `DosageSafety` is a reasonable and clinically important R6 goal. A staged alias design could preserve old instances, but maximum-dose data is safety-sensitive; allowing old and new representations together would require strict consistency rules and could leave ambiguous or conflicting limits in circulation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial less-breaking design would add `safety.doseLimit` and keep the three R4 `maxDosePer*` fields as deprecated aliases with explicit mappings. This would reduce immediate validation breaks, but it would duplicate safety constraints in the base datatype, require conflict handling when both forms are populated, and still leave edge cases such as unusual `maxDosePerPeriod` ratios, multiple same-scope limits, formula limits, and `ifExceeded` instructions that do not round-trip cleanly.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Material safety and validation tradeoffs: duplicate dose-limit representations could conflict, and not all old period ratios map cleanly to the new scoped limit model.

evidence.detail: R4 defines three top-level maximum dose fields.
R6 defines `Dosage.safety` as 0..1 DosageSafety and omits the R4 maxDosePer* fields.
DosageSafety has repeating doseLimit entries with required value and scope, optional period and text, and root `ifExceeded`.

safety.ifExceeded: Call prescriber before administering additional doses.

examples.examplesMd: The period example assumes the R4 ratio denominator can be represented as an R6 Duration. Some R4 ratios may require manual interpretation.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 maximum-dose fields were removed and replaced by a nested safety model. This is both a validation break and a safety-sensitive migration because the new model requires explicit limit scope and supports more cases than R4.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `maxDosePerPeriod`, `maxDosePerAdministration`, or `maxDosePerLifetime` are invalid as R6 Dosage JSON. R6 `safety.doseLimit` entries with `scope=dosage`, `valueInteger`, `valueExpression`, multiple limits of the same scope, per-limit text, or root `ifExceeded` cannot be represented exactly in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `maxDosePerAdministration` to `safety.doseLimit` with `scope=administration`; map `maxDosePerLifetime` with `scope=lifetime`; map `maxDosePerPeriod` with `scope=period`, converting the ratio denominator to `period` only when it is safely a duration. Flag unusual ratios, multiple limits, formulas, and exceeded-limit instructions for clinical or implementation review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer R6 safety structure is likely justified, but removal of the old fields was not the only possible path. Deprecated aliases or a profile-level transition period would have allowed old safety constraints to validate while systems adopted `DosageSafety`.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Because maximum dose limits are safety-related, mappings should be reviewed with clinical stakeholders when units, periods, or formula-based limits are not straightforward.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 had three top-level maximum-dose safety controls: per period, per administration, and per lifetime. R6 removes those names and moves dose limits into `Dosage.safety.doseLimit`, where each entry has required `value[x]` and required `scope`. The redesign is clinically richer, but the removed fields are safety-relevant and migration is not always a trivial rename, especially for period ratios and multiple or formula-based R6 limits.
keyEvidence: R4 `Dosage.maxDosePerPeriod` is 0..1 Ratio; `maxDosePerAdministration` and `maxDosePerLifetime` are 0..1 Quantity(SimpleQuantity).
R6 `StructureDefinition-Dosage.json` omits the three `maxDosePer*` fields and adds `Dosage.safety` 0..1 `DosageSafety`.

R6 `StructureDefinition-DosageSafety.json` defines repeating `doseLimit` with `value[x]` 1..1 integer, Quantity, or Expression; `scope` 1..1 required code; optional `period`, `text`, and `ifExceeded`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Although R4 Dosage is trial-use rather than normative, maximum-dose instructions are medication-safety controls. That safety role and the expert-dependent mapping cases outweigh the softening that trial-use status would otherwise provide.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `maxDosePer*` members are absent in R6; R6-to-R4 loss also occurs for new scopes, formula limits, per-limit text, multiple same-scope limits, and `ifExceeded` instructions.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A plausible less-breaking base design was to add `Dosage.safety` while retaining the three old `maxDosePer*` fields as deprecated aliases with explicit consistency rules. The tradeoff is serious because duplicate safety limits can conflict, but the alternative is still credible enough for renewed review given the safety sensitivity and non-trivial period-ratio migration.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree with the existing report's hard/high impact and partial-alternative assessment, but I place more weight on safety and expert-dependent migration than its `probably justified` rationale did.

findings.title: dose[x] and rate[x] now allow Expression

oldState.summary: Dose allowed Range or SimpleQuantity; rate allowed Ratio, Range, or SimpleQuantity.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 dose and rate choices required concrete numeric quantities, ranges, or ratios.

newState.summary: Dose and rate retain all R4 choices and add Expression.

semanticText.comment: Expression is provided for medications that are weight dependent or skin-surface-area dependent.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can carry formula-based dose and rate instructions using `doseExpression` and `rateExpression`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The paths are unchanged and the R6 type arrays add `Expression` without removing R4 types.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break because all R4 types remain valid. It is a runtime and reverse-conversion risk because R4 generated choice enums and business logic will not know `doseExpression` or `rateExpression`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Formula-based dosing can be clinically important for weight- or body-surface-area-dependent medications.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: R6 only adds `Expression` choices while retaining all R4 dose and rate types.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of representing formula-based dose and rate instructions is reasonable, and the base R6 change is a type widening that preserves R4-valid `Quantity`, `Range`, and `Ratio` content. The remaining incompatibility is reverse conversion for new R6-only `Expression` content, not avoidable R4-to-R6 breakage.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because this finding does not invalidate old R4 instances, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable under the calibration rules. An extension could carry formulas in R4 or during down-conversion, but that is an R6-to-R4 mitigation rather than a less-breaking base R6 design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed for forward compatibility; R6-to-R4 extensions or narrative are conversion mitigations, not base-design alternatives.

evidence.detail: R4 dose and rate choices do not include Expression.
R6 adds Expression to both choice type lists.

examples.examplesMd: R4 has no `doseExpression` or `rateExpression` choice members. A converter would need an extension, a rendered instruction, or manual derivation of a concrete dose.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 expands dose and rate to support expressions. This is a non-breaking widening for R4-to-R6 validation, but it is material for generated code and reverse conversion because formula-bearing R6 instructions cannot be reduced to an R4 Quantity, Range, or Ratio without evaluating or losing the formula.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 dose/rate instances remain valid by type domain. R6 instances using Expression are not valid R4 Dosage content and may fail R4 parsers, choice dispatch, schema validation, and business rules that assume numeric dose/rate values.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update R6 parsers, serializers, UI, validation tests, and dose-calculation logic to handle `doseExpression` and `rateExpression`. For R6-to-R4, preserve formulas in extensions or narrative when no safe concrete value can be derived, and require review before evaluating formulas into patient-specific quantities.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is additive in R6 and therefore relatively compatible in the forward direction. The remaining incompatibility is inherent to R4's older type domain; a cross-version extension is the least lossy fallback.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Expression language, variable context, and execution safety were not assessed.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 only widens the `dose[x]` and `rate[x]` choices by adding `Expression`; it does not remove the R4 Quantity, Range, or Ratio choices. Existing R4 dosage dose/rate instances therefore remain valid by type domain in R6. Down-converting formula-based R6 content to R4 can be lossy, but that is an expected consequence of adding a new capability rather than a reason to revisit the base R6 design.
keyEvidence: R4 `Dosage.doseAndRate.dose[x]` allows Range and Quantity(SimpleQuantity); R4 `rate[x]` allows Ratio, Range, and Quantity(SimpleQuantity).
R6 retains those types and adds `Expression` to both `dose[x]` and `rate[x]`.
R6 comments say Expression is provided for medications that are weight dependent or skin-surface-area dependent.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Trial-use status further reduces concern for an additive widening. Even with medication-safety relevance, the change does not invalidate R4 content, so FMM/status did not raise this to a standards-design concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: only new R6 `doseExpression` or `rateExpression` content lacks an R4 base choice; there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed because all R4 types are retained. R4 extensions, narrative preservation, or formula evaluation are down-conversion mitigations, not better R6 base designs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree with the existing report that this is not a hard forward break and that no less-breaking alternative is applicable, but I judge the finding as `No problem` rather than a material impact item because it is additive in R6.

findings.title: Dosage.condition adds conditional applicability not available in R4

oldState.summary: No local Dosage.condition element in R4.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had no general Dosage child for conditional applicability beyond the narrower as-needed choice.

semanticText.short: Whether the dosage applies (e.g. as a whole) (any can be true)
semanticText.definition: Whether the dosage applies as a whole. The dosage applies if any of the conditions are true.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can express conditions controlling whether the whole dosage applies.

facts.newValue: Dosage applies if any condition is true

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element is new in R6 and has no R4 path with equivalent general applicability semantics.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding an optional element does not invalidate R4 data moving to R6. It does create high reverse-conversion risk because dropping conditions can make a conditional dosage appear unconditional.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Conditional applicability can determine whether a medication instruction should be followed at all.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent dosage instructions that apply only when explicit clinical, operational, or contextual conditions are met.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: optional `Dosage.condition` is additive R6 content and does not invalidate R4 Dosage instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Representing conditional applicability is a reasonable R6 modeling goal, and adding an optional element is compatible with existing R4 data moving forward. Dropping or backporting conditions can be clinically risky, but that is a reverse-conversion concern rather than evidence that the base R6 addition should have used a different less-breaking shape.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because the new element is optional. Carrying conditions in R4 extensions or narrative may be necessary for down-conversion, but those are migration or backport strategies and should not be counted as a `Yes` alternative to the R6 base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The cost is lossy R6-to-R4 conversion policy for new conditional content, not an avoidable R4-to-R6 base-design break.

evidence.detail: `DosageCondition.code` is mandatory and preferred-bound to dosage-condition-code.

condition.text: Use this dosage only if funded or approved.

examples.examplesMd: The example is R6-only because R4 Dosage has no general `condition` container.

findings.narrativeMd: `Dosage.condition` is a new R6 capability rather than a forward break. Its importance is semantic: if a converter drops it, the remaining Dosage can look unconditional even though the R6 author made applicability conditional.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 data remains valid with respect to this addition. R6 data with `condition` is not cleanly R4-representable. Strict R4 parsers reject the field, while lossy converters that omit it can change the instruction's clinical meaning.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4, preserve conditions in an agreed extension or narrative and flag records for review when conditions affect whether therapy should occur. R6 implementations should test condition evaluation, multiple-condition OR semantics, and behavior when both `condition` and `asNeeded` are present.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A core condition element is more interoperable than extensions, so the addition is probably justified. The compatibility cost is borne by reverse conversion because R4 has no equivalent general-purpose field.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 definition says any condition can make the dosage apply; implementers should confirm how this interacts with local decision-support logic.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Dosage.condition` is new optional R6 content that states when the whole dosage applies, with any listed condition able to make the dosage applicable. It does not invalidate any R4 Dosage moving forward, but it creates a real down-conversion hazard: if the condition is dropped, a conditional medication instruction may appear unconditional. Because the element is additive and supplies a base home for clinically meaningful applicability logic, the compatibility burden appears proportionate.
keyEvidence: R6 `StructureDefinition-Dosage.json` adds `Dosage.condition` 0..* `DosageCondition` with summary flag true and definition that the dosage applies if any condition is true.
R6 `StructureDefinition-DosageCondition.json` requires `code` 1..1 and includes optional `details`, `operation`, broad `value[x]`, and `text` fields.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Trial-use status and the additive nature of the change soften the forward-compatibility concern. The judgment remains above `No problem` because conditional applicability can be clinically important when R6 content must be represented in R4.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R4 has no general Dosage condition container, so strict R4 parsers reject it and lossy converters can change meaning by omitting it.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base R6 design is necessary for R4-to-R6 compatibility because the element is optional and additive. R4 extensions or narrative are useful down-conversion strategies, but they are not alternative R6 base designs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree with the existing report's high reverse-conversion concern and no-applicable-alternative reasoning, while framing the additive base change as proportionate rather than a forward break.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, kind, type, derivation, and abstract flag are stable. Status changed from draft to active and baseDefinition changed to `BackboneType`; the base change is out of scope as inherited infrastructure.
For retained local elements, cardinalities did not materially narrow or widen. Element removals/additions and the `asNeededFor` repeatability change are covered in findings.

`text`, `additionalInstruction`, `patientInstruction`, `timing`, `route`, `method`, `doseAndRate.type`, and retained backbone support children kept their material types. Type changes for `site`, `asNeeded`, and dose/rate Expression choices are covered in findings.

Binding strengths for retained local coded elements did not become stricter. The `doseAndRate.type` ValueSet canonical changed but remains an example binding and is listed as non-breaking. No live expansions were performed.

The only material new local Dosage invariant found is `dos-1`, covered with the as-needed split. Base `ele-1`, `ext-1`, and `xpath` presentation differences are inherited or tooling-level and excluded.
No local Dosage element changed modifier status. `modifierExtension` remains the only local modifier child, inherited from the base pattern.
Summary flags for retained local elements are stable. Removed summary fields such as `sequence` and `maxDosePer*` are covered as findings.
No slicing changes were found in the Dosage elements reviewed.
No fixed values, pattern values, or defaults were found to materially change on local Dosage elements.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex changes were identified.
Dosage had no retained Reference target changes. The new `CodeableReference` BodyStructure target on `site` is covered as a type-domain finding.
No additional serialization changes beyond the reported field removals, choice split, `CodeableReference` wrapping, and new choice members were identified.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: doseAndRate.type example ValueSet canonical moved to terminology.hl7.org
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The binding strength remains `example`, so base validation does not require codes from the bound ValueSet in either version.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology clients, documentation links, and generated binding metadata may need to recognize `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/dose-rate-type` in R6 instead of the R4 `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/dose-rate-type` canonical.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: doseAndRate wording broadened to administered, to be administered, or typical amount
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element cardinality and base datatype did not change; the wording broadens context rather than imposing a new validation rule.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Review business logic that assumed `doseAndRate` always meant an actually administered amount; R6 wording explicitly includes intended or typical amounts depending on the containing resource.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Status is metadata and does not change instance validation shape.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance and maturity dashboards may treat the R6 datatype differently, but this is not an instance-level breaking change.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `Dosage` now derives from `BackboneType` rather than R4 `BackboneElement`; this inherited class-hierarchy shift should be assessed in the base datatype report.
`Dosage.safety` is the R6 replacement/expansion path for R4 maximum dose fields and needs its own datatype-level review for constraints, terminology, and conversion policy.
`Dosage.condition` introduces conditional applicability semantics and required internal fields that should be reviewed as a separate new datatype.
`DosageDetails.step` may be relevant for migrating former R4 sequence/order semantics, but it is a separate R6 datatype.
The R6 binding for `Dosage.doseAndRate.type` points to this external terminology canonical; expansion comparison was not possible from the local core package.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff or ballot change rationale was used, so justification assessments are inferred from StructureDefinition changes.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official FHIR change notes, ballot reconciliation records, or narrative diff for Dosage.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology expansions were not performed. This mainly affects confidence in value-set content equivalence for example bindings, not the structural breaking findings.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Expand and compare the relevant ValueSets with the intended terminology server versions, especially SNOMED-based example sets and the external dose-rate-type ValueSet.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: `Dosage` is usually embedded in resources. This artifact-scoped analysis did not inspect every resource or profile using Dosage, so prevalence and exact migration targets for ordering semantics are estimated.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Analyze resource-specific Dosage usages and examples in MedicationRequest, MedicationAdministration, MedicationStatement, and related profiles.
